assignments.decisiveDefect: The family declares exactly one route, obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:dcjs_correction_submission, and devotes pages 1-2 of 6 to court_transmission_correction_request, which is the primary instrument of a different declared route, obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request. Those two pages are footer-stamped 'Route: ...:dcjs_correction_submission'. In this factory's own convention the footer is a per-document route claim — rcap-ok-custom-pleading stamps eight different route footers across its 24 components — so the sentencing-court letter is wearing a route key that is not its own and that a separate live family holds a separate grant over.
assignments.theDuplicationFinding: The sibling family composed-treatment:obligation:research-decision-route:NY:ny_160_55_violation:sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request is live in MASTER_QUEUE.json at VERIFY_PENDING with its own build script and directory, and renders a 4-page packet whose pages 1-2 are the same instrument. The two letters are NOT byte-identical and not textually identical: this family's opens 'THIS IS A LETTER TO A COURT'S RECORDS OFFICE. IT IS NOT A MOTION, A PETITION OR AN APPLICATION, AND IT IS NOT FILED.' and structures the ask as numbered paragraphs 1-4 over five certificate-of-disposition blanks; the sibling's structures it as lettered sections A-C with items C1-C4. They also print different personas — this family localises to '42 Larkspur Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201', the sibling prints '42 Magnolia Street, Springfield 62704', a non-New-York placeholder, inside a New York letter. Two live families therefore ship two materially different letters asking the same office for the same act under the same statute, and no record in the repository reconciles them or says which governs.
assignments.whatIsNotWrong: Nothing measured on these six pages is legally or factually wrong, and the other fourteen obligations pass. The bound records verify byte-exact, every fee statement is verbatim from the compiled NY profile, every dotted rule is accounted for in the field map, and all six self-help stop conditions are carried. This is a boundary repair, not a rewrite.
repairOptions: Decide the boundary and record the decision. Either the DCJS family legitimately ships both steps of the recorded correction workflow — in which case its declared routeKeys must include sentencing_court_transmission_correction_request, the sibling family must be retired or explicitly subordinated, and the footers on pages 1-2 must name the route those pages actually serve — or it ships only the DCJS letter, in which case pages 1-2 come out and the participant is directed to the sibling family for step three.
Whichever is chosen, the per-document route footer on pages 1-2 must stop naming dcjs_correction_submission while rendering the sentencing-court instrument.
The two letters must not both survive in different wordings. If both families persist, one text is authoritative and the other cites it.
assignments.doNotDoThis: Do not resolve this by deleting the sibling family's grant or by editing the sibling's worktree. The sibling is a separate live subject in the claim ledger and its disposition is Captain's to order.

assignments.decisiveDefect: Two unclassified participant blanks in the rendered bytes. The caption rule 'IN THE ............................................................ COURT' is printed on page 1 of ms-99-15-59-dismissal-branch-primary-filing-1 and again on page 3 of ms-99-15-59-dismissal-branch-proposed-order-2. Neither appears in production-field-map.json (7 canonicalWrites, 12 canonicalRefusals, no court field), in reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json, or in the 'items you must supply' table of participant-instructions.md. reports/completeness-counters.json reports unclassifiedBlanks 0; the correct count is 2. participant-instructions.md compounds it by asserting 'the court's identity is a labelled blank on the petition' — the caption blank carries no label, and item C4 'What venue or agency?' is a different blank in a different section.
assignments.rootCause: Shared with id_felony_reduction-set and rcap-ok-custom-pleading. The caption is pushed into the component body as a hard-coded literal string containing the dot run, while every blank the map does account for is emitted through the {{DOTS}} token; and the blank ledger is built only from the field map's refusals ('for (const r of m.canonicalRefusals ?? []) blanks.push(row(r));', scripts/build-census-v1-composed-treatment:obligation:runtime-only:MS:uncharged-misdemeanor-immediate-dismissal-branch-99-15-59.mjs line 723). A literal dot run can therefore never be counted, classified or disclosed, and unclassifiedBlanks is structurally incapable of detecting it. The build script holds exactly 2 such literals against 13 {{DOTS}} tokens, matching the 2 caption rules in the bytes.
assignments.whyItMatters: A pleading whose caption does not name a court is not filable. This is an item the participant must supply before filing that the packet never tells them to supply.
repairOptions: Emit the caption court name through the same registered-blank mechanism as every other blank, so it acquires a field id, a disposition (REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING), a printed label, an entry in the blanks report and a row in the 'items you must supply' table.
Correct the FILING_DESTINATION sentence in participant-instructions.md, which currently tells the participant the court's identity is a labelled blank when the caption blank is not labelled.
Consider fixing the counter as well as the packet: unclassifiedBlanks cannot see a literal dot run, so the same defect will pass unnoticed on every family built to this shape.

assignments.decisiveDefect: The packet converts a sentence printed on a source-gated library form into a participant-facing requirement with denial as the stated consequence, while the family's own source-receipt.json neither names that form nor binds it by SHA-256 and still records the opposite position. The rendered page states: 'a DESPP form does impose the date, and the stated consequence of breaching it is denial. So get a criminal history record dated on or after 01/01/2024'. source-receipt.json, in the same directory at the same commit, records under whatThisReceiptDoesNotEstablish 'whether the SPBI report must bear any particular date - recorded as unresolved, not as a rule', lists only the statute and DPS-0846-C under officialSourcesRecordedInIntake, and contains no occurrence of the string 0847.
assignments.thePacketsClaimIsTrue: This is important to the repair. FABLE-VA6 read the source: private/source-imports/Expungement_AI_RCAP_Master_Library_Edition_1/STATES/CT/05_SOURCE_GATED/CT__SOURCE-GATED__DESPP-0847-C__hearing-for-clean-slate-erasure-convictions-after-1-1-2000__REV-2001-01__EN.pdf, SHA-256 08658dc45d7d41c20a26dcab54fff8756302e85bef7f4d519d9c0a3d4e4fbcfc, equal to the sha256 column of its CT STATE_MANIFEST.csv row. Its printed instruction 2 reads verbatim: 'You must submit a copy of your current criminal history record, which must be dated on or after 01/01/2024, demonstrating that such conviction has not been marked as erased. If the criminal history record is not submitted along with this form, your submission will be deemed incomplete and your request for a review and/or hearing will be denied.' The packet's quotation is accurate. The failure is the binding, not the fact.
aggravatingRecords: The CT STATE_MANIFEST.csv classes DESPP-0847-C as source_gated / disabled_pending_release_gates / source_or_currentness_gate_open, so the packet reproduces gated bytes into participant-facing text and elevates them to an instruction.

data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json, track ct-missed-erasure, still carries the withdrawn reading as a live releaseBlocker: 'The "dated on or after January 1, 2024" SPBI rule in the internal reference looks like a misreading ... Treat as unresolved rather than as a rule.'

build-findings.json and approval-request.json in the same directory DO discuss 0847-C and even flag that it is 'titled for convictions after 1/1/2000' and may not be this route's instrument, which shows the reliance was deliberate and makes the receipt's silence an omission rather than an oversight of fact.
repairOptions: Bind it. Name DESPP-0847-C in source-receipt.json with its SHA-256 08658dc45d7d41c20a26dcab54fff8756302e85bef7f4d519d9c0a3d4e4fbcfc, record that it is source-gated and that only its printed face is relied on, delete the receipt's contrary whatThisReceiptDoesNotEstablish entry, and retire the corresponding releaseBlocker in the track registry — so the packet's claim rests on hashed bytes that staleness detection can reach.
Or withdraw it. Take the requirement back to the registry's recorded 'unresolved rather than a rule' position and remove the instruction from the packet.

Do not leave it as it stands, where a participant-facing requirement carrying a denial consequence rests on unbound, unhashed, gated bytes that the family's own source record says do not establish it.
